name: trama
description: See your System as a layered Model of state machines, review Proposals and Drifts, and steer your coding agent from one editor tab.

trama.agentCommand.markdownDescription: Command that starts your coding agent in a terminal. `{prompt}` is replaced by the shell-quoted prompt; if it is missing, the prompt is appended. Examples: `claude {prompt}`, `codex {prompt}`. Trama never calls a model itself.

enumDescriptions: Run `#trama.agentCommand#` in a terminal (omp, claude, codex, copilot CLI, cursor-agent…).
Send the prompt to the agent chat built into the editor (Copilot in VS Code). In Cursor, or if the chat is not available, the prompt is copied to the clipboard.
trama.agentLauncher.markdownDescription: Where the Design, Scan and Run buttons send their prompt.

trama.autoScan.markdownDescription: After you approve a Proposal, launch the agent to Scan the Features it touched. With the terminal launcher it only applies when `#trama.agentCommand#` is set.

trama.skillsDir.markdownDescription: Folder, relative to the project root, where **Trama: Initialize Project** installs the agent skills. Use `.claude/skills` for Claude Code.

languageModelTools.name: trama_view
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Shows part of the project's Trama Model, the source of truth for how the software behaves. Without `ref`: the System, its Actors and Features. With `ref`: that element with its States, Transitions (condition and consequence in prose), Events and who receives them. Element reference: `checkout` (Feature), `order` (Machine), `user` (Actor), `order/Paid` (State), `order/Paid/user.CANCEL` (Transitions on an Event), `user.CANCEL` (Event).

languageModelTools.name: trama_paths
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the simple paths between two States of one Machine, shortest first, with the Event and prose of each step.

languageModelTools.name: trama_analyze
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Warnings about the Model: unreachable States, non-final States with no way out, Events nobody receives. For one Machine or the whole System.

machine.description: Machine ID; omit for the whole System

languageModelTools.name: trama_search
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Case-insensitive search over names and prose of the whole Model; each hit with its element reference.

languageModelTools.name: trama_board
languageModelTools.modelDescription: The work board: open Proposals and Drifts waiting for the developer's decision, then Tasks to do, in progress and done.

languageModelTools.name: trama_validate
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks the Model's internal consistency, or the Model with an open Proposal applied. Never looks at code.

proposal.description: Proposal ID; omit to validate the current Model

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_new
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Opens a new Proposal: the only way to change the Model. Then write each changed Model file with trama_proposal_write. Only the developer can approve it.

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_write
languageModelTools.displayName: Trama: Write a Model file in a Proposal
languageModelTools.userDescription: Write a Model file in a Proposal
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Writes the complete new version of one Model file inside an open Proposal (the Model itself is untouched until the developer approves). `path` is relative to `.trama/model/`, e.g. `checkout/order.md` or `actors/user.md`. Returns the validation of the Model with the Proposal applied.

content.description: The complete file in the Trama Model format

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_delete_file
languageModelTools.displayName: Trama: Delete a Model file in a Proposal
languageModelTools.userDescription: Delete a Model file in a Proposal
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Marks a Model file for deletion in an open Proposal. `path` is relative to `.trama/model/`.

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_show
languageModelTools.modelDescription: A Proposal: status, whether it is stale, its structural changes, validation, and the developer's feedback if it was rejected.

languageModelTools.name: trama_task_new
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Creates a Task in To do. A Task references the Model elements it implements in `refs`, unless it is technical (no behaviour change, no refs). The body says in domain words what must be true when done.

refs.description: Model elements the Task covers. Element reference: `checkout` (Feature), `order` (Machine), `user` (Actor), `order/Paid` (State), `order/Paid/user.CANCEL` (Transitions on an Event), `user.CANCEL` (Event).

technical.description: True for work that changes no behaviour (refactor, dependencies); then refs must be empty

drift.description: ID of the Drift this Task resolves, if any

body.description: What must be true when done, in domain words

languageModelTools.name: trama_task_show
languageModelTools.modelDescription: A Task with the current Model text of every element it references.

languageModelTools.name: trama_task_move
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Moves a Task to `todo`, `doing` or `done`. Move it to `doing` when you start and to `done` when the behaviour matches the Model.

languageModelTools.name: trama_drift_new
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Records a Drift: the code differs from the Model in a way that would change the Diagram. File it exactly once. If the code handles an important case the Model forgot, first open a Proposal and pass its ID in `proposal`. Only the developer resolves Drifts.

refs.description: The Model elements closest to the difference. Element reference: `checkout` (Feature), `order` (Machine), `user` (Actor), `order/Paid` (State), `order/Paid/user.CANCEL` (Transitions on an Event), `user.CANCEL` (Event).

proposal.description: ID of a Proposal that would fix the Model, if the code is right

body.description: What the code does, what the Model says, where in the code

languageModelTools.name: trama_drift_show
languageModelTools.modelDescription: A Drift with its references and its attached Proposal, if any.
